component.name: ByteKeys
component.summary: Keyboard lighting, fans and performance modes for your laptop

description.p: ByteKeys is a control center for Linux laptops, like the vendor apps on Windows. It controls the keyboard lighting (plain white backlights as well as single-zone, multi-zone and per-key RGB keyboards), the performance modes, the fan curves and the battery charge limit. It detects your laptop and keyboard automatically and configures itself.

ul.li: Live temperatures, fan speeds and battery at a glance
Performance modes, and custom fan curves that the laptop's firmware runs (ASUS)
Full fan speed and battery charge limits
Brightness, colors, zones and per-key colors; hardware and software effects
The laptop's vendor app key (Armoury Crate, NitroSense, OMEN...) can open ByteKeys
Automations: dim on battery, turn off when idle, low battery and overheat warnings, Caps Lock indicator, schedules
Profiles you can switch from the tray, the command line or automations
Works with kernel drivers, common USB lighting controllers and OpenRGB

screenshot.caption: Home: temperatures, fans, performance mode, keyboard and battery
Lighting: live preview, effects and colors
Performance: modes, fan curves and battery care
Automation: lighting that reacts on its own

description.p: A control center for the whole laptop, in a new look:

ul.li: Home dashboard with live temperatures, fan speeds, performance mode, keyboard and battery
Performance modes, custom firmware fan curves per mode (ASUS), full fan speed and battery charge limits
The vendor launch key (Armoury Crate, NitroSense, OMEN...) opens ByteKeys
Redesigned lighting page with animated effect previews and a color wheel

description.p: First public release: automatic detection, modes and effects, zones and per-key colors, rules, profiles, tray icon, command line tool and background service.
